title: Adaptive training load optimization for sprinters via offline reinforcement learning and multi-modal physiological feedback.
abstract: Elite sprint training requires daily adjustment of training load to balance performance adaptation and fatigue, yet physiological monitoring does not necessarily translate into a specific next-session prescription. This study formalizes daily sprint training prescription as a finite-horizon Markov Decision Process and develops an adaptive load-optimization framework that couples multi-modal physiological feedback with offline reinforcement learning (RL). A 19-dimensional state fusing autonomic, neuromuscular, endocrine, subjective, and load-aggregate signals is encoded by a dual-tower network [a one-dimensional convolutional neural network-Transformer temporal branch and a multi-layer perceptron (MLP) static branch] over an action space of 62 admissible training-type/intensity/volume combinations. A composite reward penalizes overreaching while rewarding short-term gain, longitudinal adaptation, and acute-to-chronic workload ratio conformity. The policy is learned by conservative off-policy training on retrospective data, evaluated through the Fitted Q-Evaluation (FQE) and Doubly Robust (DR) estimators, and presented to coaches as the three leading candidate actions, with SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) values used to explain the model's preferences among the candidate actions. In a 12-week single-center retrospective comparison of 70 national-level sprinters (35 men and 35 women; 100 m personal best (PB) ≤ 11.20 s for men or ≤ 12.50 s for women), grouped by whether their squad had adopted the tool (n = 35 RL-guided) or continued classical block periodisation (n = 35 control), the RL-guided cohort demonstrated between-cohort differences of +0.240 s in 100 m [95% confidence interval (CI) +0.128 to +0.352; p < 0.001, d = 1.00], +0.104 s in 30 m (p < 0.001, d = 1.00) and +2.17 cm in countermovement jump (p < 0.001, d = 1.01). Zero algorithmically defined sustained multi-indicator fatigue/load events were observed in the RL-guided cohort vs. seven in the control cohort (1.43 per 1,000 athlete-days); these events should not be interpreted as clinically diagnosed overtraining syndrome. Off-policy evaluation yielded exploratory point estimates whose precision remains unknown because uncertainty intervals were not calculated. These observational findings describe associations with an RL-guided, coach-in-the-loop workflow and do not establish a causal effect of the RL policy.

title: Sports Trauma in Athletes with Impairment.
abstract:
PURPOSE OF REVIEW: Trauma in athletes with impairment is an under-reported aspect of Para sport. This review article aims to present current data regarding characteristics of acute sports trauma in winter and summer Para sport participants and considerations for management of acute injury. This includes recommendations for trauma prevention and preparedness, assessment and management on the field of play, and extrication from Para sport equipment.
RECENT FINDINGS: Injury surveillance systems help characterize risk factors for acute sports trauma and inform injury prevention programs. Concussion and injuries to the head and face are common in Para sport. Winter sports such as Para alpine skiing and sled hockey have high rates of acute sports trauma. While summer sports generally have higher rates of repetitive use injuries, some sports such as blind football, Para cycling, wheelchair rugby, judo, and goalball have higher rates of acute traumatic injuries. There are many important factors to consider when assessing field of play, extrication, emergency evaluation, and care-coordination considerations. title: Patient-Reported Outcomes Plateau at 1 Year Compared With 2 Years After Open Proximal Hamstring Repair.
abstract:
PURPOSE: To determine whether there is a significant difference between 1- and 2-year postoperative patient-reported outcome measures (PROMs) after proximal hamstring repair (PHR).
METHODS: This retrospective study used data from an institutional registry of patients who underwent PHR between October 2021 and December 2023 with a minimum follow-up of 24 months. Patients who completed preoperative and 1- and 2-year postoperative surveys were included in this study. PROMs included the Lower Extremity Functional Scale, the Hip Outcome Score, the Perth Hamstring Assessment, and the 12-Item Short Form Survey. Cohort-specific minimal clinically important difference was calculated. Return to sport and surgical satisfaction were included as secondary outcomes. Univariate analyses compared clinical outcomes.
RESULTS: Sixty-two of 84 eligible patients met the inclusion criteria for this study, with a mean follow-up time of 23.2 months (range 22.4-24.8). No significant differences were found between 1- and 2-year PROMs after PHR (P > .05). There were no statistically significant differences in the proportion of patients who achieved minimal clinically important difference at 1 year versus 2 years postoperatively, and these differences remained nonsignificant after disaggregating the data by sex (P > .05). After 1 year postoperatively, there were no significant additional improvements in the ability to return to sport (P = .371), sport level (P > .99), or percentage of return to sport (P = .961).
CONCLUSIONS: No significant differences were found between 1- and 2-year PROMs after PHR. PROM scores, minimal clinically important difference achievement rates, return to sport, and surgical satisfaction outcomes were stable from 1 to 2 years postoperatively, with no clinically meaningful improvements observed in the second postoperative year.
LEVEL OF EVIDENCE: Level IV, retrospective case series.

title: Supervised Combined Exercise as an Intervention in Treatment-Resistant Depression: A Mixed-Methods Case Report.
abstract:
UNLABELLED: Treatment-resistant depression (TRD) remains a severe clinical condition associated with persistent symptomatology, functional impairment, and unhealthy lifestyle patterns. This case report examines the effects of a supervised combined exercise intervention using a mixed-methods approach. A 55-year-old woman with a 13-year history of TRD treated with clomipramine (150 mg/day), lamotrigine (400 mg/day), and bromazepam (3 mg/day) presented with moderate depressive symptoms (Montgomery-Åsberg Depression Rating Scale [MADRS] = 28; Clinical Global Impressions Scale [CGI-S] = 4), marked sedentary behavior (approximately 13 h/day), low cardiorespiratory fitness (CRF) (VO2peak = 18 mL·kg-1·min-1), and elevated fat mass (42%). She participated in a 12-week supervised combined exercise programme (aerobic and resistance training, twice weekly) within the TRACE-RMD framework. Following the intervention, depressive symptoms decreased by 57% (MADRS = 12), with remission of global illness severity (CGI-S = 1) and a 16.7% increase in CRF. Functional disability and perceived stress were substantially reduced, while perceived social support markedly increased, as assessed by the Sheehan Disability Inventory (the global score reflects disability, item 4 reflects perceived stress, and item 5 reflects social support). Qualitative narratives indicated improvements in mood regulation, reduced rumination, increased self-efficacy, and enhanced social reintegration. Supervised combined exercise may represent a feasible and clinically meaningful adjunctive intervention in TRD, acting not only on symptom reduction but also on functional recovery and psychosocial re-engagement. Further controlled studies are warranted.

title: Understanding Sleep in Ultramarathon Runners: An Exploratory Assessment during a Training Week.
abstract: Sleep plays a vital role in sports performance. Ultramarathon runners may experience impaired sleep during training and competition; however, further investigation is needed. The current study aimed to evaluate sleep in ultramarathon runners during a typical training week. We evaluated 15 male athletes with a mean age of 45.1 ± 10.5 years and a mean ultramarathon experience of 6.37 ± 6.49 years. Sleep was assessed using the Munich Chronotype Questionnaire, the Morningness-Eveningness Questionnaire, the Pittsburgh Sleep Quality Index, the Athlete Sleep Behavior Questionnaire, the Epworth Sleepiness Scale, and a 7-day sleep diary. Most participants were morning chronotypes (86.7%), and the mean social jetlag of was 0.60 ± 0.69 hour. The athletes went to bed and woke up earlier on workdays than on free days ( p = 0.002). Most athletes reported < 8 hours of sleep per night, 53.3% reported poor sleep-related behaviors, and 46.7% were classified as poor sleepers; however, 73.3% did not report excessive daytime sleepiness. These findings suggest a heterogeneous and multidimensional sleep-health profile in ultramarathon runners.

title: Voluntary wheel running attenuates mechanical hypersensitivity but transiently prolongs gait impairments in male and female mice with unilateral osteoarthritis.
abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Physical activity is a first-line therapeutic intervention for managing osteoarthritis-related pain and functional impairment. However, the growing literature questions the long-term relevance of exercise-induced improvements in patients, while pre-clinical research evidence-base is limited by reliance on stressful, forced exercise paradigms which do not reflect voluntary engagement. Here, we investigated the effects of voluntary wheel running on the pain experience in mice with joint pain.
DESIGN: We investigated the impact of free access to a running wheel on sensory, functional and affective outcomes following unilateral intra-articular injection of monoiodoacetate (MIA) into the knee joint of 8-week-old male and female C57Bl/6J mice (n=14/16). Mice were single-housed and randomly assigned to remain sedentary or have unrestricted access to a wheel from at least two weeks before MIA. Behavioural outcomes were assessed longitudinally over an eight-week post-injection period.
RESULTS: Mean daily running distance decreased from 3.01 to 0.69 km in males and from 3.90 to 1.69 km in females by day 5 after MIA. Following a short-lived recovery, males showed a progressive decline, while the rebound in activity was sustained in females throughout the observation period. Voluntary wheel running attenuated MIA-induced secondary mechanical hypersensitivity, with higher mechanical withdrawal thresholds in active than sedentary mice, most obviously during the pain-like maintenance stage (day 40: males: 0.08g; 95%CI 0.040 to 0.126; females: 0.125g, 95%CI 0.029 to 0.222). Conversely, wheel running transiently delayed full gait recovery, with between-group differences in stance symmetry and duty factor during early recovery in both sexes (males day 20: stance: -11.8%; 95%CI -21.25 to -2.27; duty factor: -5.4%; 95%CI -10.53 to -0.35; females day 12: stance: -22.0%; 95%CI -32.48 to -11.51; duty factor: -15.9%; 95%CI -22.97 to -8.83). Finally, wheel access had little effect on anxio-depressive-like behaviours or cognition, but reduced faecal output and influenced body weight.
CONCLUSIONS: In this animal model of MIA-induced osteoarthritis, voluntary wheel running was associated with improvements in secondary mechanical hypersensitivity, despite a transient and acute worsening of several gait impairments. These findings highlight the importance of assessing multiple behavioural domains in preclinical studies and underscore the complexity of exercise-induced effects on pain and function.

title: Delayed Diagnosis of Achilles Tendon Rupture in a 75-Year-Old Patient with Bimalleolar Ankle Fracture: A Case Report.
abstract:
CASE: A 75-year-old woman sustained a minimally displaced bimalleolar ankle fracture after a fall. An ipsilateral Achilles tendon rupture was missed until day 26, when persistent heel pain and inability to plantarflex prompted an MRI, revealing a rupture with a 5.5-cm gap. Both injuries were treated nonoperatively using controlled ankle motion (CAM) boots, heel wedges, progressive weight bearing, and rehabilitation. At 12 months, the patient had resumed independent ambulation.
CONCLUSION: All ankle fracture patients should undergo systematic Achilles tendon assessment with early follow-up reassessment and a low threshold for advanced imaging when the initial examination is limited.

title: Collective case study on periodized training in elite female middle- and long-distance swimmers preparing for national competition.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Elite swimmers increasingly face calendars requiring multiple performance peaks within a single season, a scenario for which traditional single-target periodization models may be insufficient.
METHODS: This longitudinal collective case study followed five elite female middle- and long-distance freestyle swimmers across a 52-week macrocycle preparing for two national championships. The program combined three altitude camps, sea-level integration phases and two timed tapers. Training intensity distribution (TID) was quantified with a three-zone lactate-threshold model; hemoglobin, hematocrit, red blood cell count, creatine kinase and cortisol were measured at four time points; and performance was assessed by time-trial and official competition results. Given N = 5, analysis prioritized a smallest-worthwhile-change (SWC) classification for performance and paired effect sizes with 95% confidence intervals for blood markers rather than null-hypothesis significance testing. Hematological outcomes are concentration-based indices; training-load descriptors refer to in-water swimming only.
RESULTS: Applying an SWC of ≈0.24% to the 20 athlete-by-event observations, 12/20 (60%) changes at Competition 1 and 18/20 (90%) at Competition 2 exceeded the SWC, most representing improvement over baseline; this ordering held across the full defensible range of reference variability (SWC 0.22-0.42%). Hematological effect sizes were largest at Week 27 (RBC: Hedges' g = 2.32, 95% CI [0.64, 4.01]; HCT: g = 2.04 [0.50, 3.58]), while creatine kinase and cortisol peaked at Week 17 and were closer to baseline at Week 49, compatible with a lower physiological stress state at that sampled time point. TID shifted across phases (pyramidal during base development, polarized during altitude blocks, threshold-oriented during race-pace sharpening), with marked inter-individual heterogeneity in performance and physiological responses.
CONCLUSION: Across this double-peak macrocycle, most athlete-by-event changes exceeded the SWC, and the proportion doing so was higher at the second championship than at the first; these changes occurred alongside altitude-associated increases in concentration-based oxygen-transport indices and a taper-associated normalization of creatine kinase and cortisol. With no control group or randomization, only five athletes and four blood samples, several simultaneous interventions and unmeasured confounders (iron status, menstrual-cycle phase, dryland load), these findings describe associations only. They are offered as exploratory, hypothesis-generating observations from a single elite squad rather than as causal evidence.

title: The Sleep and Diet of Elite Female Australian Rules Football Athletes Differ With Age and Season Phase.
abstract: The Australian Football League Women's (AFLW) competition is comprised of a short, intensive competitive season, highlighting the importance of proper fuelling and recovery to support performance. Little is known about the dietary and sleep habits of AFLW athletes across a season, and the influence that age has on these behaviours. Therefore, this study aimed to determine the effects of season phase and age on dietary intake and sleep in elite AFLW athletes. Dietary intake and sleep were assessed in 22 AFLW athletes (25.9 ± 5.0 y) over 10 nights, including five consecutive nights during both pre-season and in-season. Dietary intake was quantified through self-reported food diaries using a smartphone application (Easy Diet Diary), and sleep via a wearable monitoring device (Oura ring). Restricted maximum likelihood mixed models were used to determine variations in dietary intake and sleep in AFLW players between season phases (i.e., pre-season vs. in-season) and age. In-season protein (115.15 ± 35.14 vs. 126.48 ± 40.10 g, p = 0.026) and fat intakes (72.93 ± 29.55 vs. 83.43 ± 33.14 g, p = 0.012) were significantly lower compared to pre-season, with no differences in sleep measures observed between season phases. While age did not influence dietary intake, each additional year of age was associated with 8 min less sleep (p = 0.001) and 4 min earlier wake times (p = 0.032). These findings suggest that protein and fat intakes fluctuate across the seasons, with increasing age being a non-modifiable risk factor for shorter sleep durations within AFLW athletes.

title: Gender Differences in Sports Injuries of the Foot and Ankle.
abstract: This article examines sex-based differences in foot and ankle injuries among female athletes, emphasizing the role of anatomic, hormonal, biomechanical, and sociocultural factors. Female athletes are disproportionately affected by ankle sprains, chronic instability, and bone stress injuries. Conditions such as relative energy deficiency in sport and the female athlete triad contribute to injury risk and long-term health consequences but remain under-recognized. This article highlights disparities in research, treatment, and outcomes, calling for improved screening, sex-specific prevention strategies, and greater inclusion of female subjects in sports medicine research to inform evidence-based care and optimize outcomes for female athletes.

title: Chitosan hydrogels: Crosslinking mechanisms, environmental adaptability, and sports-health relevance.
abstract: The development of extreme-environment sports health interfaces is shifting from short-term signal detection toward long-term interfacial service, where the reliable performance of chitosan (CS) hydrogels depends on maintaining interfacial coupling, signal transduction, and biological function under low-temperature exposure, immersion, salt-rich sweat, and dynamic wound conditions. The protonatable amino groups of CS chains serve as crosslinking sites, cationic interfacial moieties, and structural contributors to antibacterial and hemostatic activity, while hydroxyl-mediated hydration, dynamic networks, and multicomponent modification support wet adhesion, deformation recovery, and tissue repair. In winter sports, underwater and sweat-rich exercise, and sports-related wound management, the bottleneck is not a single deficiency in mechanics, conductivity, or adhesion, but coupled failure: salt-rich sweat and immersion induce charge screening, low-temperature exposure and osmotic stress disturb hydrated networks, and repeated deformation drives conductive/adhesive pathway reconstruction, leading to signal drift and impaired repair. This review summarizes chemical and physical crosslinking strategies for CS hydrogels, clarifies the roles of carbon-based materials, metal/metal-oxide nanocomponents, and natural biomacromolecules in conductive pathway formation, network reinforcement, wet interfacial regulation, and bioactive repair, and discusses environmental adaptability and sports applications. Future directions toward long-term stability, multifunctional integration, standardized evaluation, and service reliability under realistic use conditions are proposed.

title: Open and closed-chain shoulder joint position sense: inter-day reliability and normative profiles in male contact sport athletes.
abstract: The purpose was to determine inter-day reliability and normative values for open and closed-chain shoulder joint position sense (JPS). Male contact and collision sport athletes (18-40 years) participated in two study phases. Sixteen athletes completed open- and closed-chain JPS tests on two occasions (2-9 days apart) to determine inter-day reliability. Twenty-eight athletes completed the same protocol on one occasion to establish normative profiles. Open-chain JPS was assessed in a standing position using shoulder flexion to pre-defined angles with a laser pointer (55°, 90° and 125° of humerothoracic flexion; no haptic target); closed-chain JPS was assessed in a push-up position by reproducing target positions (chest lowered onto a hurdle at 16.5 cm [low] or 30.5 cm [high]; an initial haptic target). Three-dimensional kinematics quantified repositioning errors. Intraclass correlation coefficients (ICC) and standard error of measurement (SEM) were calculated for reliability. Pearson correlations were calculated between open and closed-chain errors. Open-chain tests demonstrated moderate reliability across both arms (ICCs = 0.71-0.74), with better reliability on the dominant limb (ICCs = 0.68-0.90) compared to the non-dominant (ICCs = 0.43-0.55). SEM values ranged from 0.70 to 2.03°. Closed-chain tests showed poor reliability at the high target (ICC = 0.49) but good reliability at the low target (ICC = 0.81, SEM = 10.2 mm). Normative data indicated greater repositioning errors at low targets in open-chain tasks and at high targets in closed-chain tasks. Correlations between open- and closed-chain errors were weak to absent. Open-chain JPS testing demonstrated acceptable reliability, whereas closed-chain reliability was dependent on target height. The two tasks appear to assess distinct aspects of proprioception. The open-chain test reflects predominantly single-joint (glenohumeral) position sense, whereas the closed-chain test reflects multi-joint, composite position sense. These findings establish initial reference values for JPS in male contact athletes.

title: Comparative Plasma Proteomics of Arabian and Thoroughbred Racehorses at Rest and During Early Recovery from Training and Racing.
abstract: Breed-associated differences in the plasma proteome of Arabian and Thoroughbred racehorses at rest and during early recovery from training and racing remain incompletely characterised. Tandem mass tag (TMT)-based liquid chromatography-tandem mass spectrometry (LC-MS/MS) plasma proteomics was performed on samples from 43 Thoroughbred and Arabian racehorses collected at rest and 30-40min post-exercise during early-season training, mid-season training, and racing. Breed and sex effects were tested with false discovery rate correction within each contrast and an effect-size threshold (absolute fold change >= 1.20); age and race placing were evaluated by breed- and time-specific Spearman correlations. More proteins met the reporting criteria for between-breed differences during initial training and racing than during mid-season training. Across the analysed contrasts, proteins with higher relative abundance in Arabians included FETUB, CNTN1, FGFR1, HGFAC and C4BPA, while proteins with lower abundance included ENPP5, SMPDL3B, KRT8 and KRT19. Age was associated with the plasma abundance of proteins annotated to coagulation, lipid transport, immune regulation and extracellular matrix-related functions. More proteins met the reporting criteria for sex-associated differences at rest than during early recovery. Exploratory associations with race placing were detected for two proteins in Thoroughbreds after exercise, with none meeting the reporting criteria in Arabians. These findings identify breed-associated plasma protein differences and candidates for independent validation.

title: Running the Numbers: High Metabolic Load Distance as an Alternative to Traditional External Load Metrics in Elite Women's Football.
abstract: This study examined the relationship between High Metabolic Load Distance (HMLD) and both session RPE (sRPE) and athlete wellness in women's football and compared it with traditional load monitoring metrics. An observational design was used to collect data from one elite women's football team during training and games in the 2024/25 A-League W season. Twenty-four athletes wore global positioning devices to capture external load metrics, including total distance (TD), high-speed running distance (HSRD) and HMLD. Session RPE and daily wellness were collected through online questionnaires. Generalised additive models were used to examine non-linear relationships between external load, subsequent days' wellness and RPE, and relationships between morning wellness and same-day external load. Higher load was associated with increased sRPE, and poorer next-day wellness, with effects diminishing within two to 3 days post-session. Across all outcomes, HMLD demonstrated stronger and more consistent relationships than TD and HSRD, explaining a greater proportion of variance in wellness and sRPE. Same-day wellness was associated with differences in distances, with higher motivation and lower fatigue corresponding to higher HMLD. HMLD demonstrated comparatively stronger associations with immediate perceived exertion and short-term athlete reported wellness than traditional distance-based metrics in this cohort. These findings support the application of HMLD as a practical and sensitive measure to inform training decision-making in elite women's football.

title: Shoulder Arthritis.
abstract: Glenohumeral osteoarthritis is a common, debilitating joint disease characterized by progressive cartilage loss, subchondral bone remodeling, and capsular stiffness, leading to pain, restricted motion, and functional impairment. Diagnosis relies on both clinical evaluation and imaging studies. Classification systems, such as the Walch classification, assist in assessing disease severity and guiding treatment decisions. Management begins with conservative approaches, including nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drugs (NSAIDs), physical therapy, and intra-articular injections, progressing to surgical interventions such as total or reverse shoulder arthroplasty for advanced disease. Early diagnosis and patient-specific treatment are essential to ensuring optimal patient outcomes.

title: Associations between countermovement jump impulse and running kinetics following ACL reconstruction.
abstract: Persistent deficits in lower-limb loading are commonly observed following anterior cruciate ligament reconstruction (ACLR) and may influence running biomechanics. Countermovement jump (CMJ) impulse can provide a phase-specific measure of force-time characteristics to reflect limb loading capacity; however, its relationship with running kinetics remains unclear. This study aimed to quantify phase-specific CMJ impulse following ACLR and examine associations with vertical ground reaction force (vGRF) metrics during treadmill running at the return-to-running phase. Forty-two participants performed three unilateral and bilateral CMJs on dual force plates and ran at 8 km/hr on an instrumented treadmill. Concentric, eccentric braking, and landing impulses were calculated. Running variables included weight acceptance rate, weight acceptance peak force, and maximum applied force. Inter-limb differences were assessed using Wilcoxon/paired t-tests. Impulse-vGRF relationships were analysed using Pearson/Spearman correlations and multiple linear regression. The ACLR limb exhibited significant deficits across all unilateral and bilateral CMJ phases, except for unilateral landing impulse. Deficits were greatest for unilateral concentric impulse (Δ1.3Ns·kg-0.67, d = 1.49, p < 0.001). Maximum applied force limb symmetry index (LSI) was explained by unilateral concentric impulse LSI (adjusted R2 = 0.25, p < 0.001). Maximum applied force of the affected limb was explained by unilateral concentric impulse (adjusted R2 = 0.38, p < 0.001). Weight acceptance peak force of the affected limb was explained by unilateral concentric and landing impulses (adjusted R2 = 0.37, p < 0.001). No meaningful relationships were observed for eccentric impulses or weight acceptance rate metrics. These findings indicate that jump impulse testing may provide clinically relevant indicators of running kinetics.

title: Exercise-related signal abnormality (ERSA)-associated acute thigh muscle injuries in a subset of professional soccer players.
abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Exercise-related signal abnormality (ERSA) is a relatively new MRI entity described in professional soccer players. We report a subset of players who sustained acute muscle injuries and ERSA lesions in the same muscle.
MATERIALS AND METHODS: A retrospective review was conducted from July 2024 to July 2026 to identify all MRI studies of professional soccer players with an acute thigh muscle injury and ERSA lesion in the same muscle. Anatomical site, laterality, ERSA lesion subtype and length, and acute muscle injury grade as per the British Athletics Muscle Injury Classification (BAMIC) were recorded.
RESULTS: There were 18 ERSA-associated acute thigh muscle injuries in 16 soccer players (12 males, 4 females; median age 20.5 years). Affected muscles were the rectus femoris (n = 12), adductor longus (n = 5), and semitendinosus (n = 1). Type C ERSA lesions (n = 13) and BAMIC grade 2b (n = 8) muscle injuries were the most common. All acute muscle injuries were located within the ERSA lesions. No intratendinous extension was observed. Median ERSA lesion length was 21.5 cm and median acute muscle injury length was 7.0 cm. The main ERSA-associated muscle injury patterns were pre-degloving (n = 6) and myofascial (n = 6) injuries of the rectus femoris and distal myotendinous junction injuries of the adductor longus (n = 4).
CONCLUSION: We describe a new muscle injury pattern, termed ERSA-associated acute thigh muscle injuries, in a cohort of professional soccer players. Distinct injury patterns were observed in the rectus femoris and adductor longus.

title: Acute lower leg compartment syndrome as a result of calf strain due to a skiing injury.
abstract: Acute compartment syndrome (ACS) of the lower leg is a limb-threatening condition that requires urgent management. It is most commonly caused by direct trauma, such as high-speed motor vehicle accidents or blunt force injuries, including those seen in earthquake victims. Lower extremity ACS most commonly occurs in the setting of a tibial fracture. ACS can also occur as a result of non-contact injuries, such as muscle strain during athletic activities. Early clinical suspicion and close monitoring are critical, as the most telling symptom is pain. Neurovascular signs typically appear later in the progression of the condition. While imaging tools like ultrasound and MRI may help identify muscle tears and large haematomas, they are not diagnostic for ACS. When the clinical picture is unclear, compartment pressure measurement can aid diagnosis—particularly in settings where access to surgical intervention is limited and transportation decisions are challenging. We present an unusual case of ACS in the leg following a muscle injury sustained during skiing. The patient’s severe pain, along with physical findings of increased calf diameter and ultrasound-confirmed haematoma, was a key factor prompting transfer to a higher-level care facility for urgent fasciotomy.

title: Limb ischemia-reperfusion injury in rats is partially mediated by enhancing necroptosis via phosphorylation of RIPK1 and MLKL.
abstract: Limb ischemia-reperfusion injury (L-IRI) causes severe skeletal muscle damage and functional impairment through activation of regulated cell-death and inflammatory pathways. Necroptosis is a regulated form of necrotic cell death mediated through the receptor-interacting protein kinase 1 (RIPK1)-RIPK3-mixed lineage kinase domain-like protein (MLKL) signaling axis. Prior experimental studies have shown that Necrostatin-1 (Nec-1) attenuates acute skeletal muscle ischemia-reperfusion injury in rats. However, how Nec-1-sensitive protection relates to RIPK1/MLKL-associated signaling, circulating muscle injury markers, inflammatory responses, histological damage, and functional recovery during the early postischemic period remains incompletely defined. In this study, we used a rat model of unilateral hindlimb ischemia involving 3 h of ischemia followed by reperfusion for up to 7 days to evaluate these interrelated responses. Nec-1 was administered before ischemia and after reperfusion. L-IRI resulted in elevated plasma creatine kinase and lactate dehydrogenase levels, severe histopathological injury, increased TUNEL staining, impaired grip strength, and reduced Modified Tarlov scores. These changes were accompanied by increased phosphorylation of RIPK1 and MLKL, activation of inflammatory signaling pathways, and altered expression of injury-associated inflammatory mediators. Nec-1 treatment reduced RIPK1/MLKL-associated signaling, inflammatory mediator expression, circulating muscle injury markers, and histological injury while preserving muscle architecture and improving functional recovery. These findings support and extend previous evidence that Nec-1-sensitive necroptosis-associated signaling contributes to early skeletal muscle injury following L-IRI. Pharmacologic targeting of regulated necrotic and inflammatory pathways warrants further investigation as a potential adjunct strategy for limiting acute skeletal muscle injury after limb reperfusion.NEW & NOTEWORTHY This study links Necrostatin-1 (Nec-1)-sensitive receptor-interacting protein kinase 1 (RIPK1)/mixed lineage kinase domain-like protein (MLKL)-associated signaling with biochemical, histological, inflammatory, and functional outcomes after rat hindlimb ischemia-reperfusion injury. Nec-1 reduced RIPK1 and MLKL phosphorylation, muscle injury, and early functional impairment. These findings extend prior skeletal-muscle studies by integrating molecular pathway activation with longitudinal functional recovery while supporting a contribution of RIPK1-associated necroptotic signaling.

title: Immunomodulatory and Antioxidant Biomimetic Hydrogel Coloaded with Glycyrrhizic Acid and Copper Gallate for Synergistic Cartilage Regeneration.
abstract: Articular cartilage lesions are persistently restrained by three interwoven pathological drivers: chronic inflammatory response, sustained oxidative stress, and progressive extracellular matrix (ECM) catabolism. Coupled with the inherently weak self-repair capacity of hyaline cartilage, effective therapeutic interventions for such injuries remain an unmet clinical demand owing to the inherently poor self-repair capacity of hyaline cartilage, effective therapeutic interventions remain an unmet clinical demand. Herein, we engineered a biomimetic composite hydrogel designated ECM/HAMA/GA@Cu-GA, which integrates decellularized cartilage extracellular matrix, methacrylated hyaluronic acid (HAMA), glycyrrhizic acid (GA), and copper gallate (Cu-GA). This integrated hydrogel platform simultaneously endows biomimetic mechanical support, potent anti-inflammatory and antioxidative bioactivities, as well as robust chondrogenic induction capacity. In vitro cellular evaluations verified the outstanding biocompatibility of the composite hydrogel. The biomaterial efficiently polarizes macrophages toward the anti-inflammatory M2 phenotype, suppresses the secretion of pro-inflammatory mediators and matrix-degrading proteases, and facilitates the migration and chondrogenic differentiation of bone marrow mesenchymal stem cells (BMSCs). Transcriptomic profiling suggested that its underlying molecular mechanisms may involve activation of the PI3K/Akt signaling cascade and blockade of the NF-κB-mediated inflammatory pathway. In vivo assessments using rat articular cartilage defect models demonstrated that the ECM/HAMA/GA@Cu-GA hydrogel achieves satisfactory synchronous regeneration of hyaline cartilage and subchondral bone at 4 and 8 weeks post-implantation, with superior regenerative performance relative to all control groups. Collectively, this multifunctional hydrogel enables comprehensive remodeling of the pathological joint microenvironment with favorable biosafety profiles, representing a translatable candidate strategy for clinical management of cartilage degenerative disorders.

title: Satellite Cells as Regulators of the Skeletal Muscle Microenvironment: Evidence Beyond Fusion.
abstract: Wedged between the sarcolemma and basal lamina, satellite cells (SCs) are resident skeletal muscle stem cells responsible for regeneration following injury. SCs share this microenvironment with fibrogenic, immune, vascular, and neural cell populations. Accumulating evidence indicate that SCs do more from this position than regenerate muscle. Activated SCs participate directly in extracellular matrix (ECM) remodeling and signal to fibroblasts and fibro-adipogenic progenitors (FAPs) through miRNA-containing extracellular vesicles (EVs). SCs also reside near capillaries, where reciprocal signaling with endothelial cells stimulates angiogenesis and in return influences myofiber adaptation. SCs are also localized at the neuromuscular junction (NMJ), where they secrete proteins implicated in synaptic remodeling. During regeneration, SCs share their environment with infiltrating immune cells, and while the influence of macrophages on SCs is well established, the reciprocal direction remains comparatively unexplored. EV transport has emerged as one candidate mechanism for part of this influence, operating independently of SC-myofiber fusion. However, supporting evidence is stronger for fibroblasts and FAPs than for endothelial cells and is currently absent for NMJ, immune cells, and non-myogenic fate transitions. The consequences of losing SCs are evident in SC depletion models, where muscle develops excess collagen, blunted capillary expansion, and NMJs that regenerate poorly and degenerate prematurely with age. Whether SCs also transition to fibrogenic or adipogenic fates in aged and dystrophic muscle remains less clear. This review highlights non-canonical roles of SCs and evaluates fusion-independent communication, including SC-derived EVs, as a candidate mechanism linking SCs to the fibrogenic, immune, vascular, and neural compartments of muscle.

title: Ethanol-induced alterations in mesenchymal stromal cells and the effects of aspalathin: implications for alcohol-associated osteonecrosis.
abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Alcohol-associated osteonecrosis is a debilitating condition characterized by progressive bone destruction. Although mesenchymal stromal cells (MSCs) play a critical role in tissue repair, the effects of chronic alcohol exposure on MSCs and their responsiveness to microenvironmental signals remain unclear.
METHODS: MSCs were exposed to ethanol (EtOH) to evaluate changes in viable cell number, ROS-related fluorescence signals, and the expression of mitochondrial-related, senescence-associated, and chemokine signaling-related molecules. CXCL12 expression was examined in human femoral head specimens and ethanol-exposed osteocyte-like cells. The effects of aspalathin (ASP) on EtOH-induced alterations in MSCs were also investigated.
RESULTS: EtOH exposure reduced viable MSC number and increased ROS-related fluorescence signals. It was also associated with decreased expression of ATP5A and CXCR4 and increased expression of p16. CXCL12 expression was higher in alcohol-associated osteonecrosis tissue than in osteoarthritis tissue and appeared qualitatively increased in ethanol-exposed osteocyte-like cells. These findings indicate altered CXCL12 and CXCR4 expression across the tissue and in vitro experimental settings. ASP treatment attenuated the EtOH-induced reduction in the CCK-8 signal, was associated with attenuation of ROS-related fluorescence signals, significantly restored ATP5A expression, suppressed p16 expression, and showed a non-significant trend toward recovery of CXCR4 expression.
CONCLUSIONS: Ethanol exposure was associated with alterations in the cellular state of MSCs, accompanied by changes in ROS-related fluorescence signals and the expression of mitochondrial-related, senescence-associated, and chemokine signaling-related molecules. ASP partially attenuated some of these ethanol-induced alterations. Further studies are required to clarify the functional significance of these findings and to validate them in vivo.

title: Psychological Profiles of Elite Cerebral Palsy Football Players: Comparison With Able-Bodied Athletes.
abstract: The purpose of this study was to examine the psychological profiles of elite cerebral palsy (CP) football players associated with athletic performance. While understanding psychological competencies is vital for high-performance para-sports, data on specific adaptive strategies remain scarce. This study compared 16 elite CP football players with 1,460 able-bodied athletes across four competitive levels (Regional-International) using the JISS-Psychological Test for Elite Athletes, which assesses 10 factors across three categories: psychological skills, self-understanding, and athletic commitment. CP players showed moderate-to-large effects in Imagination and Self-Analysis compared with athletes at all competitive levels (Hedges' g = 0.58-0.98, adjusted p < .05). These findings suggest that elite athletes with CP develop superior internal cognitive strategies to compensate for physical and environmental constraints, such as spasticity and motor uncertainty. The results highlight the importance of psychological support focused on internal simulation and self-reflection to enhance competitive excellence in para-sports.

abstract: Metabolic bone health is crucial for the overall well-being of female patients. Any discussion of female BMD and metabolic bone health must include the female triad.

title: Intermittent fasting enhances muscle regeneration via an EDA2R-NIK-myomixer axis.
abstract: Skeletal muscle exhibits a remarkable regenerative capacity that relies on adult stem cells known as satellite cells (SCs), which differentiate into myogenic progenitors to drive muscle repair. How varying energy availability alters myogenesis, however, remains unknown. Here, we demonstrate that intermittent fasting (IF) in mice upregulates a myogenic gene program, including Myomixer, a muscle-specific fusogen that facilitates the merging of progenitor cells into myofibers. IF enhances the regeneration of injured muscles by expanding the SC population and promoting the proliferation and fusion of myogenic progenitors. These effects are absent in an SC-depletion model. We show that fasting-induced EDA2R-NIK signaling increases Myomixer expression and fusion in myoblasts. Notably, mice lacking EDA2R or NIK fail to respond to the myogenic effects of IF. Furthermore, our data suggest that mice with Duchenne muscular dystrophy also benefit from an IF regimen. Therefore, IF-induced regeneration holds potential for aiding recovery from muscle damage.

title: Age-Dependent Alterations in Glutathione Metabolites Following Muscle Injury.
abstract: Age-related impairments in antioxidant defences contribute to delayed tissue repair and increased susceptibility to oxidative stress following muscle injury. Glutathione (GSH), a key cellular antioxidant, plays a central role in redox homeostasis and recovery processes. GSH is synthesized through a sequential process involving glutamic acid and cysteine, catalyzed by the rate-limiting enzyme glutamate cysteine ligase (GCL) to form γ-glutamyl cysteine (γGC), which subsequently combines with glycine to produce GSH. Using metabolomic profiling and acute skeletal muscle injury in mice, this study characterized age-dependent alterations in GSH biosynthesis. Clustering analysis identified that muscle from 12-month-old mice have a delayed GSH synthesis profile in response to injury compared to 3-month-old mice, with an age-dependent delay in γGC accumulation. This suggests that aging negatively influences metabolite profiles within the GSH synthesis pathway. As γGC lies downstream of this enzymatic step, its supplementation may bypass the GCL bottleneck. To test this, C2C12 myoblasts were treated with γGC (from 1-100 µg/mL), however this did not affect myoblast proliferation or differentiation. These data suggest detrimental age-related dysregulation of GSH-related metabolites in skeletal muscle repair, particularly γGC, however further examination of the role of exogenous γGC supplementation in this process is required to identify further therapeutic benefit.
journal: Canadian journal of physiology and pharmacology

title: Growth factor printing into fusing cell spheroids to engineer spatially complex tissues.
abstract: Cell spheroids are powerful building blocks for tissue engineering. To create spatially heterogeneous, native-like tissues, typically individual stem/progenitor cell-derived spheroids are primed toward specific phenotypes prior to assembly into larger tissues. However, this pre-specification impairs spheroid fusion into scaled-up, cohesive tissues due to secretion of boundary proteins around individual spheroid peripheries over time. In this study, we report a bioprinting platform for spatially patterning growth factors into an immature living matrix of spheroids to locally direct cell fate in situ. Laponite-containing bioinks supported sustained delivery of transforming growth factor-beta 3 (TGF-β3) into a bath of immature mesenchymal stromal cell-derived spheroids, resulting in superior chondrogenesis compared to standard media supplementation. When TGF-β3 and bone morphogenetic protein 2 were patterned into an initially phenotypically homogeneous living tissue matrix, an osteochondral-like gradient developed over time in culture. This bioprinting platform enables spatially complex tissue engineering with potential applications in musculoskeletal tissues and beyond.

title: Analytical strategies for distinguishing endogenous and exogenous anabolic androgenic steroids in doping control.
abstract: Doping control for anabolic androgenic steroids (AASs) must separate endogenous physiology from exogenous administration when the same molecular entities occur on both sides of the boundary. This Critical Review evaluates analytical strategies for that source-attribution problem, with emphasis on urinary steroid profiling, longitudinal interpretation, compound-specific isotope ratio mass spectrometry, intact phase-II metabolites, alternative matrices, high-resolution mass spectrometry (HRMS), and data-driven evidence integration. Current practice relies on a staged logic: routine steroid-profile measurements define marker behavior, the steroidal module of the Athlete Biological Passport (ABP) evaluates individual changes, and gas chromatography-combustion-isotope ratio mass spectrometry (GC-C-IRMS) supplies orthogonal source evidence when pseudo-endogenous steroids or atypical profiles require confirmation. UDP-glucuronosyltransferase 2B17 (UGT2B17) deletion, sex, menstrual-cycle phase, pregnancy, medication, and sample degradation can alter marker concentrations and ratios. Intact conjugates, dried blood spots (DBS), HRMS metabolite discovery, and statistical tools can provide additional evidence, but their performance depends on validation for the relevant matrix and administration scenario. The most defensible strategy is therefore a tiered framework that combines longitudinal interpretation, source-specific chemical evidence, and expert review.

title: Evaluation of a four-herb Chinese medicine formula at different concentrations on muscle damage and inflammation in a rat model of DOMS.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Delayed onset muscle soreness (DOMS) impairs exercise recovery, while current treatments remain limited. Traditional Chinese Medicine (TCM) formulas may provide safe, multi-target interventions.
OBJECTIVES: This study evaluated the dose-dependent protective effects of a four-herb Chinese medicine formulation (safflower, Chinese Angelica, peach kernel and myrrh) against DOMS in a rat model.
METHODS: Thirty-two male SPF SD rats were randomly allocated to control or low- (1696 mg/kg), medium- (3392 mg/kg), or high-dose (6784 mg/kg) groups. The formulation was administered orally for 11 days, with DOMS induced by exhaustive swimming on day 8. Serum CK, Mb, CRP, IL-6, and PGE2 were measured at baseline and at 24, 48, 72, and 96 h post-exercise.
RESULTS: The medium- and high-dose groups exhibited significantly lower serum CK, Mb, CRP, IL-6, and PGE2 levels than controls, with the high-dose group showing the largest reductions. The low-dose group showed limited or no significant reductions in most markers, demonstrating a clear dose-dependent protective effect.
CONCLUSIONS: The formulation dose-dependently attenuates muscle damage and inflammation in a rat DOMS model, with high-dose treatment achieving the fastest recovery. Clinical trials are warranted to confirm the efficacy and safety in humans.

title: Effects of Intramuscular Mesenchymal Stem Cell and Boric Acid Administration on Muscle Damage and Recovery in an Exhaustive Swimming Rat Model.
abstract: Exhaustive exercise induces damage to skeletal muscle, reducing athletic performance and delaying recovery. Effective experimental strategies are needed to mitigate this damage and accelerate tissue regeneration. This study aimed to address limitations in the therapeutic efficacy of bone marrow-derived mesenchymal stromal/stem cell-like cells (MSCs) associated with limited cell viability by evaluating boric acid (BA) as an antioxidant and metabolic modulator to enhance cell viability and muscle repair. Twenty-five female Wistar albino rats underwent a 15 day exhaustive swimming protocol and received intramuscular injections of MSCs (1 × 106 cells), BA (10 µg), or their combination, according to the experimental group allocation. Bone marrow obtained from five additional donor rats was used exclusively for MSC isolation and culture. Daily exhaustion time, serum biomarkers lactate, lactate dehydrogenase (LDH), creatine kinase (CK), and gastrocnemius histology were evaluated. Intramuscular BA improved endurance and reduced biochemical markers of muscle injury, whereas MSC application promoted structural muscle regeneration, as evidenced by centrally located nuclei and improved muscle fiber integrity. Combined MSCs + BA treatment improved several biochemical and histological outcomes compared with exercise alone. Serum lactate concentrations remained elevated in treated groups 24 h after the final exercise session, indicating altered post-exercise metabolic responses. Overall, intramuscular BA modulated metabolic responses, whereas administration of bone marrow-derived stromal/stem cell-like cells was associated with structural regeneration in this rat model of exercise-induced skeletal muscle injury, providing a reproducible platform for evaluating regenerative interventions.

title: Early Diagnosis and Therapeutic Evaluation of Rheumatoid Arthritis by a Mitochondria-Targeted Near-Infrared Fluorescent Probe.
abstract: As a chronic autoimmune inflammatory ailment, rheumatoid arthritis (RA) presents with persistent synovitis and progressive destruction of cartilage and bone structures, for which early diagnosis and real-time evaluation of therapeutic responses remain significant clinical challenges. Dysregulation of the inflammatory microenvironment, especially mitochondrial dysfunction accompanied by abnormal elevation of mitochondrial viscosity, is closely associated with RA progression. However, current imaging techniques are still insufficient for real-time visualization of these subcellular changes during disease development and treatment. Herein, we present a mitochondria-targeted near-infrared fluorescent probe, YJ-1, constructed based on a donor-π-acceptor (D-π-A) framework for sensitive detection of viscosity variations and dynamic RA imaging. YJ-1 exhibits excellent selectivity toward viscosity changes, efficient mitochondrial localization, and a strong near-infrared emission at 764 nm, enabling high-contrast and low-background imaging. Moreover, the probe demonstrates outstanding photostability, low cytotoxicity, and good biocompatibility. Owing to these advantages, YJ-1 enables real-time visualization of mitochondrial viscosity changes in living cells, zebrafish, and mouse models. In addition, in a λ-carrageenan-induced inflammatory mouse model, YJ-1 successfully monitors disease-associated mitochondrial viscosity alterations and dynamically evaluates mesenchymal stem cell (MSC)-mediated immunoregulatory therapy. Collectively, YJ-1 provides a robust imaging platform for exploring mitochondrial microenvironment dynamics during RA progression and offers a promising strategy for assessing therapeutic efficacy in inflammatory diseases.

title: GW9508 suppresses chondrogenic differentiation of BMSCs and attenuates heterotopic ossification without significantly affecting osteogenic differentiation.
abstract: Post-traumatic heterotopic ossification (HO) is a pathological bone-forming disorder characterized by aberrant activation of bone marrow-derived mesenchymal stem cells (BMSCs) and ectopic endochondral ossification; however, effective targeted therapies remain limited. This study investigated the regulatory effects and underlying mechanisms of GW9508, an agonist of free fatty acid receptors GPR40/120, on HO progression. After determining the safe concentration range of GW9508 using a CCK-8 assay, in vitro chondrogenic and osteogenic differentiation models were established to evaluate its effects on BMSC lineage commitment through qRT-PCR, Western blotting, and histological staining. A C57BL/6 mouse Achilles tendon transection model was further used to assess in vivo efficacy by micro-computed tomography, histological analysis, and immunofluorescence staining. GW9508 did not affect BMSC proliferation but significantly reduced the expression of chondrogenic markers Sox9, Col2a1, and Acan at both mRNA and protein levels in a dose-dependent manner, accompanied by decreased cartilage extracellular matrix deposition. In contrast, GW9508 showed no significant effects on osteogenic markers Runx2, ALP, and Sp7 or mineralized nodule formation. In vivo, local administration of GW9508 reduced ectopic bone formation and inhibited both early chondrogenesis and subsequent ossification. Collectively, these findings suggest that GW9508 attenuates HO progression by suppressing the chondrogenic differentiation of BMSCs, thereby limiting the subsequent endochondral ossification process. Under the present in vitro experimental conditions, GW9508 selectively inhibited chondrogenic differentiation without causing significant alterations in osteogenic differentiation. These findings provide new insights into potential therapeutic strategies for post-traumatic HO.

title: DNA-adsorbing nanozyme hydrogel reprograms the immuno-oxidative microenvironment to support stem cell-based cartilage repair in osteoarthritis.
abstract: Osteoarthritis (OA) is a prevalent degenerative joint disease, and stem cell therapy is often limited by a hostile joint microenvironment. Excessive reactive oxygen species (ROS) and damage-associated cell-free DNA (cfDNA) cooperatively drive innate immune activation, inflammatory macrophage polarization, and chondrogenic instability, forming an immuno-oxidative barrier to cartilage repair. Here, we developed a bioactive DNA-adsorbing nanozyme hydrogel (MNKB/HA) to remodel this niche and enhance BMSC-mediated cartilage repair. MNKB/HA integrates Mn3O4 nanozymes with Kartogenin (KGN)-engineered bone marrow mesenchymal stem cells (BMSCs) in an injectable hyaluronic acid matrix. Mn3O4 exhibited SOD- and CAT-like activities, scavenging O2·-, H2O2, and ·OH, while efficiently adsorbing cfDNA and CpG-ODN to suppress TLR9/MyD88 signaling and M1 polarization and promote M2 polarization. In vitro, 10 μg/mL Mn3O4 was cytocompatible, protected BMSCs and chondrocytes from H2O2-induced apoptosis, and reshaped inflammatory secretion, with IL-10 increased 8.3-fold and TNF-α, IL-6, and IL-1β reduced. KGN stabilized the chondrogenic phenotype (SOX9, COL Ⅱ, ACAN), while its combination with Mn3O4 synergistically enhanced chondrogenic stability under oxidative/inflammatory stress. In rat OA, intra-articular MNKB/HA reduced OARSI scores, restored COL II and ACAN, decreased MMP13, improved subchondral bone microarchitecture, and attenuated synovitis and osteophytes. MNKB/HA also reduced synovial cfDNA, weakened TLR9 signaling, promoted M2 polarization, and showed intra-articular retention for at least 10 days without notable systemic toxicity. Thus, MNKB/HA remodels the immuno-oxidative niche through synergistic ROS scavenging and cfDNA adsorption, providing a strategy for stem cell-mediated cartilage repair in OA.
